stories.title: Iranian man barely survives bombing, but wants war to go on
stories.summary: An Iranian man who was buried under rubble in US Israel bombing campaign says he wants the war to go on, and destroy the regime.

stories.title: Election day confusion in Louisiana after voting changes
stories.summary: The governor of Louisiana canceled the U.S. House primaries after tens of thousands of votes had already been cast. On Election Day, we hear from voters trying to make sense of the last-minute changes.

stories.title: San Francisco celebrates iconic peace activist Wavy Gravy's 90th birthday
stories.summary: The peace activist, counterculture icon and philanthropist known as Wavy Gravy turned 90, and San Francisco threw a big party.

stories.title: What motivated Chinese-born Uyghers to fight in Syria's civil war
stories.summary: Thousands of Chinese-born Uyghur fighters fled China to fight in the Syrian civil war. They say generations of political persecution in China motivated them to take up arms.

stories.title: Prayer festival calls for more religion in politics, not less
stories.summary: A prayer festival on the National Mall in Washington, DC was partially organized and funded by the federal government. Its evangelical messaging called for more religion in politics not less. Critics are concerned about an erosion of the wall between church and state. NPR's Emily Feng went to the event to understand the audience and appetite for this approach.

stories.title: What scientists are learning about geoengineering from satellite pollution
stories.summary: Professor Eloise Marais from the University College London talks about her research on pollution from satellites and its impact on earth's climate.
